rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The extraction vocabulary in one pass: an **ore** is a mineral worth mining (bauxite, not clay); **gangue** is the worthless rock riding with it; a **flux** is added to bind that gangue — acidic silica for basic impurities, basic limestone (→ CaO) for acidic silica — into a fusible, floating **slag** (CaSiO₃ in the iron furnace).…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂ (basic flux from limestone) - CaO + SiO₂ → CaSiO₃ (slag) - brass = Cu + Zn; bronze = Cu + Sn; stainless steel = Fe + Cr + Ni + C - Na–Hg + H₂O → NaOH + Hg + ½H₂ (amalgam decomposed by water)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Covers only: introduction of ores, gangue or matrix, flux, slag (within Chemistry of Metals).  ·  Out of scope here: topics of neighbouring units in Chemistry — don't mix them.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "A flux is a substance that combines with the gangue of an ore to form a fusible slag."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***The blast furnace's limestone*** — every tonne of iron needs ~0.25 t of limestone: not for the iron, but to carry the sand away as CaSiO₃ slag; without it the furnace chokes on pasty silica.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Vocabulary of Extraction Before any metal flows, the ore must be described: what mineral it is, what worthless rock travels with it (**gangue**), what is added to make the impurities flow (**flux**), what the flux turns them into (**slag**), and what metals are blended into alloys.…  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Ore, mineral, gangue - A **mineral** is any natural compound of a metal; a **mineral becomes an ore** when the metal can be extracted profitably. - **Gangue (matrix)** is the worthless sandy/rocky material mixed with the ore — silica, clay, limestone. Concentration removes most of it; the flux deals with the rest.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Acid gangue -> basic flux (CaCO3); basic gangue -> acidic flux (SiO2). Alloys: brass=Zn, bronze=Sn, stainless=Cr(+Ni). Amalgam = Hg partner; iron the exception.

rows.text: **Verified PYQ NEB 2024 (2m): Write the composition of brass, bronze, and stainless steel, with one use of each.** — **Brass** is copper alloyed with zinc (about 60–90 % Cu, remainder Zn); it machines well and has a gold-like appearance, so it is used for musical instruments, fittings and cartridge cases.…  ·  **NEB-style (2m): What is a flux? Give one acidic and one basic flux with the gangue each removes.** — A **flux** is a substance added to the concentrated ore during smelting to combine with the gangue and form a low-melting, immiscible **slag** that floats on the metal and can be drawn off.…

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: For alloy questions, NEB wants composition + one use of each — name alone scores half; quote percentages where known (bronze ~88/12).

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Flux chemistry is just acid-base neutralisation at 1500 C: acidic oxides pair with basic oxides; the salt they form must melt, float and not dissolve in the metal — three physical demands on top of the chemistry.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Ore = mineral extracted profitably (bauxite yes, clay no). Gangue/matrix = worthless rock (silica, clay). Flux binds gangue into slag: acidic flux SiO2 removes basic gangue; basic flux CaCO3 -> CaO removes acidic gangue, iron furnace: CaCO3 -> CaO + CO2, CaO + SiO2 -> CaSiO3 slag.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Slag is not waste: ground blast-furnace slag is a cement ingredient, and slag wool is insulation — the by-product outsells some metals by tonnage.

rows.text: ## 3. Scientific Definitions | Term | Scientific meaning | Example | |---|---|---| | **Ore** | Mineral from which metal is extracted profitably | Haematite Fe₂O₃ | | **Gangue (matrix)** | Worthless rocky impurity in the ore | Silica, clay | | **Flux** | Substance added to fuse with gangue | CaCO₃ (basic), SiO₂ (acidic) | | **Slag** | Fusible product of flux + gangue | CaSiO₃ |…  ·  ## 4. Detailed Explanation ### 4.1 How flux chooses its gangue - Chemistry of pairing: an acidic oxide neutralises a basic one. Iron ore carries silica (acidic) → basic flux CaO (from limestone) snares it into calcium silicate slag. If the gangue were basic (lime), the flux would be acidic sand.…  ·  ## 5. rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Explain why sodium is handled as sodium amalgam rather than as the free metal.  ·  ## 6. Common Confusions **Flux is not fuel:** the flux does not burn or reduce anything — it only chemically binds the gangue into a fusible slag. The coke both heats and reduces; the limestone only cleans.  ·  **Slag is not dross:** dross is oxide scum floating on a melt; slag is the deliberate flux+gangue product with a controlled composition (CaSiO₃).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Amalgam ≠ alloy with any liquid:** an amalgam is specifically with mercury; brass in mercury is not an amalgam.  ·  ## 7.
